reason: The cited evidence (E1–E4) describes the alloy's initial single-phase FCC state, its high SFE, active dislocation motion, and severe lattice distortion near grain boundaries, but it does not report any strain-rate-dependent tests, grain-boundary precipitation or ordering, or a ductile-to-brittle transition. The key mechanistic premises about high-strain-rate-induced pile-up triggering secondary phases and toughness loss are therefore unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: High strain rate causes dislocation pile-up at grain boundaries in this HEA
Pile-up creates local stress concentration and increased strain energy
This triggers nucleation of secondary precipitates or ordering at grain boundaries
Such grain-boundary phases reduce stress distribution and cause ductile-to-brittle transition
